svg.title: Baraza architecture — memory with due process
svg.desc: The user's session turns (and a synthetic document corpus kept as an eval harness) flow into claim extraction: every preference, rule or judgment becomes a claim with a mandatory verbatim quote and a turn anchor selected from a closed set. Claims are appended to an append-only Firestore event log whose deployed rules reject update and delete. On each write, contradiction detection retrieves a blocked, temporally gated set of at most twenty claims about the same subject — the user — and adjudicates in one bounded call. A fold over the log produces the disputed ledger, the agenda, and the doctrine, which is compiled from committed beliefs only and carries rule-to-claim provenance. The partner session runs under the doctrine, agenda-led, and raises a divergence card when the user's statements collide. The approval gate — promotion-isolated, holding no model — is the sole writer of claim.committed; rejection retracts permanently. A dashed visibility boundary marks the one readable_by predicate in front of the public dossier surface. Cloud Scheduler fires the reconcile Job through the OIDC-guarded baraza-trigger hop; every scheduled event is labelled as scheduled.
svg.text: Baraza — memory with due process
claim → append-only log → fold → doctrine · contradiction detection on write, on the user, never a sweep · no belief acts unratified
Model roles, not model IDs — pins live in src/baraza/schema/models.py and nowhere else; the README's Google Cloud table records the live-verified IDs once.
SOURCES
Your session turns
anchor grammar turn:t-N · subject: the builder
Document corpus — eval harness
synthetic · chat export, scanned PDF, XLSX, DOCX
SCHEDULED INITIATION
Cloud Scheduler — nightly
fires on schedule; never counted as organic activity
baraza-trigger — Cloud Run service
OIDC-guarded hop: Scheduler → service → jobs.run
adopted after the direct path 403'd (STOPPED-DEPLOY.md)
reconcile Job — Cloud Run
re-detects over claims since its last recorded pass
regenerates the agenda · appends session.proposed
one outbound notification — the agent speaks first
every event marked scheduled=True — labelled, never organic
appends
1 · Claim extraction — MODEL: GEMINI fast role
every preference, rule and judgment becomes a Claim — quote mandatory, verbatim
anchor SELECTED from a closed set, never generated · fabricated anchor = stop condition
targets judgment shape: conditions, thresholds, exceptions — a way of thinking, not a tone slider
claim.asserted — visibility defaults private
APPEND-ONLY EVENT LOG · Firestore
create-only writes · deployed rules reject update and delete — verified live
event IDs are content hashes, so a retried Job appends nothing twice
fixing bad data means appending a superseding event, never editing one
on each claim written
2 · Contradiction detection — on write, on YOU
block: subject ∪ object entities ∪ predicate_hint
subject = the user entity · aliases resolved at query time
temporal gate — epoch interval overlap, integers only
cap at MAX_RETRIEVED = 20
ONE bounded call — MODEL: GEMINI reasoning role
all-pairs at ~3,000 claims = 4,498,500 comparisons — refused;
on-write blocking makes it one bounded call per claim
contradiction.detected
fold over the log
ordered by (occurred_at_millis,
event_id) — integers, never strings
disputed ledger
your statements that collide, both quoted
agenda — no human wrote it
each item cites its ledger entry
resolved items retire themselves
DOCTRINE — the operating policy
compiled from COMMITTED beliefs only
rule ← claim provenance on every rule: same doctrine,
every rule cited · compilation replays byte-identically
refuses to pick between conflicting committed rules —
a conflict becomes a divergence card, never a silent overwrite
the session runs under the doctrine
3 · Partner session — Cloud Run service, private
agenda-led working session: drafting interleaved with elicitation
session N+1 is shorter than session N — retirement events link them
THE DIVERGENCE CARD
"On turn t-14 you said 'never send before I've seen it' [quote].
Just now: 'just send the routine ones' [quote]. Which governs?"
refuses to silently overwrite the old rule until adjudicated
session.turn appended BEFORE the next turn is solicited
APPROVAL GATE — no model, not an agent
the ONLY writer of claim.committed · batch ratification at session end
rejection retracts permanently: retrieval, ledger, agenda, next doctrine
visibility chosen explicitly — the default stays private
promotion and the visibility choice are distinct events,
so the disclosure decision is auditable separately
promotion-isolated
ingest and reconcile never import
the approval module · deployed rules
deny the event type on create ·
a unit test asserts the negative ·
agent fleet has transfer disabled —
no agent can hand work to it
claim.committed · claim.visibility_set · contradiction.resolved → next fold → next doctrine
THE VISIBILITY BOUNDARY — beliefs about you are private by default
every read path
readable_by(claim, audience)
defined ONCE — src/baraza/schema/visibility.py
the quote is reachable only through quote_for(audience);
the raw field raises at the access site, and the build
fails if it is named outside the schema package
fails CLOSED on unknown audience or visibility
an unreadable claim may be COUNTED toward a contradiction,
never quoted · RedactedClaim is the only thing that crosses
an item with unreadable sides is downgraded, never dropped
dossier surface — Cloud Run, the public route
reads only claims committed AND readable by the asking audience
committed is the retraction axis; visibility is the disclosure axis
the Dossier view: every belief, its quote, the moment it was learned,
one click to reject — the retraction is itself an append-only event
uncited synthesis → refusal, with its own acceptance criterion
withheld counts are honest; withheld contents are not disclosed
a fresh deployment shows a logged-out judge nothing at all —
that is the boundary working, not an empty database
Doctrine compilation is the deterministic part; model compliance with a cited rule is a measured number with provenance (docs/metrics.json), never an assertion.
